newsitem.title: POLAND: STOMIL SEES '96 PAYOUT AT PLN 0.4/SHARE.
newsitem.headline: STOMIL SEES '96 PAYOUT AT PLN 0.4/SHARE.

text.p: The management of Polish tyre maker Stomil Olsztyn SA wants to set the firm's 1996 dividend at 0.4 zloty per share, the company's financial director said on Friday.

"As far as the dividend is concerned, the general shareholders' meeting will make a decision in the second half of May...the management has recommended earmarking 40 groszes (0.4 zlotys per share," Bohdan Stankiewicz told a news conference.
He said Stomil, which netted 56.9 million zlotys last year, was likely to slightly increase the profit in 1997.

"This (1997) is not a year, in which Stomil and also other companies, will try to push hard for the financial result. They will focus on expenses needed to strengthen marketing and on investment, which will be a burden for financial results," Stankiewicz said.
French tyre maker Michelin has 52.1 percent of shares in Stomil, based in north-eastern city of Olsztyn.

The firm's trade director Zbigniew Kosacki, also present, said the company planned to increase its passenger car tyre market share in Poland to more than 30 percent in 1997 from last year's 26 percent.
He said the company would also try to defend its 80-percent market share in tractor tyres, but this would be difficult.
Kosacki also urged the government to ban imports of used tyres, which he said posed a threat to traffic safety and cost Poland jobs in tyre industry.--Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
